working_title: Yorkshire's East Coast Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing Bridlington, Flamborough, Filey and Scarborough
angle: The Yorkshire coast is one of England's most overlooked golf destinations, stringing together a compact cluster of genuinely varied clubs — clifftop links, hybrid layouts and one famous inland course — all within easy driving distance of each other. The post makes the case for building a two- or three-night golf trip around this stretch, with honest notes on what each club actually offers visitors.
research_notes:
- Yorkshire Union of Golf Clubs has 191 affiliated clubs; the county stretches from the North Sea to near Blackpool, with 'quality and quantity' per Bunkered
- Bridlington Golf Club (Belvedere): James Braid design, opened 1905; par 72, c.6,708 yards from white tees; semi-private, visitors welcome; nestled between the Yorkshire Wolds and the North Sea
- Bridlington Links Golf & Leisure Estate: separate venue, par 72, c.6,719 yards, 'distinctive links feel', cliff-top holes along Danes Dyke, views over Bridlington Bay
- Golf Coast Passport covers Bridlington Belvedere, Bridlington Links, Flamborough Head, Filey and Hornsea — good value multi-round option for visiting groups
- Flamborough Head Golf Club: founded 1931; 18-hole cliff-top links, par 71, c.6,185–6,244 yards; 'moulded around the contours of the famous headland'; visitors welcome every day (advance booking essential); the Old Beacon (built c.1674, only known example in England) sits beside the 5th tee; the club brands itself 'Friendliest Club on the Coast'
- Filey Golf Club: established 1897; 18-hole course blending links and parkland styles; panoramic views over the North Sea; visitors welcome; equipment hire available
- Scarborough South Cliff Golf Club: cliff-top course, 18 holes; mix of parkland and cliff-top holes; good facilities including clubhouse dining and pro shop
- Ganton Golf Club (15–20 min inland of Scarborough): founded 1891 by Tom Chisholm; par 71 (some sources say 72), 7,055 yards from championship tees; rated one of the top 3 courses in Yorkshire alongside Alwoodley and Moortown; hosted 1949 Ryder Cup, 2000 Curtis Cup, 2003 Walker Cup; only inland course to host the Amateur Championship (1964, 1977, 1991); design shaped by Harry Vardon, James Braid, JH Taylor, Harry Colt, Alister MacKenzie and Tom Simpson; sandy subsoil gives genuine links character despite being inland; tight bents-and-fescue fairways, deep bunkers, dense gorse; WHS handicap index required to play; visitors can book via club office; Dormy House on-site accommodation available
- Coastal wind is a meaningful factor throughout this stretch — club selection and shot shape matter more than on inland courses
- Getting there: A64 corridor links York/Leeds to Scarborough area in roughly 1.5–2 hrs from most of the North of England; no direct rail to Flamborough or Filey without a drive from Scarborough/Bridlington station
- Note: specific current green fees for Flamborough and Filey not confirmed in research — avoid stating precise figures; Ganton high-season visitor fees have been quoted in older sources (2023 data) so treat as indicative only and advise readers to check directly
